To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the equipower property holds for the combination-based permutation tests and that the dependency structure of the data affects the power behavior of the combined tests.

(i) permutation tests are equipower, at least approximately; (ii) the power behavior is essentially the same for the combination of two unidimensional tests and for the combination of the corresponding V-dimensional tests, provided that the correlation structure of the variables in the two samples is the same.

(i) permutation tests are consistent, even if the sample size is small, provided that a sufficient number of informative variables are available; (ii) the equipower property is preserved in presence of correlation, provided that the number of variables is sufficiently large; (iii) the power behavior in the presence of correlation depends on both the number of variables and the number of samples.
